subject.title: 2026.7.1 gateway crash-loop: legacy memory sidecar `meta`/`chunks` conflicts are fatal while `files` conflicts auto-resolve

question: Which legacy Memory Core tables may use canonical-wins conflict resolution, and what proof is required before a content-bearing `chunks` sidecar can be archived?
rationale: Metadata and derived-cache conflicts can plausibly prefer canonical state, but chunk conflicts may represent distinct user memory; the permanent persisted-state policy cannot be selected safely from implementation mechanics alone.

options.title: Use table-specific conflict rules
options.body: Treat duplicate metadata and derived cache identities as canonical-wins, while preserving strict verification or explicit reconciliation for content-bearing chunks.

options.title: Make all canonical rows authoritative
options.body: Resolve every sidecar conflict by retaining canonical rows and archiving the legacy database, accepting the possibility that divergent legacy chunks are discarded.

options.title: Keep strict conflicts, improve recovery
options.body: Continue blocking on every non-file conflict but add an explicit Doctor flow that explains, backs up, and resolves the sidecar with user confirmation.

recommendation.title: Use table-specific conflict rules
recommendation.body: Treat duplicate metadata and derived cache identities as canonical-wins, while preserving strict verification or explicit reconciliation for content-bearing chunks.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal is ownership of the merged Memory Core SQLite migration and its conflict contract.
